# Fictional transcript editing example

Illustrative invented text. There is no corresponding audio fixture and no speech-recognition test claim.

## Rough draft

00:08 — We can send the draft on Friday if the product name is confirmed. I think the name is Cedar or Seeder. Let's ask Jo.

00:22 — Okay, I'll ask Jo today. The final copy is not approved yet.

## Checked reading-copy example

00:08 — We can send the **draft** on Friday **if the product name is confirmed**. The product name is **[unclear — check 00:08]**. We will ask Jo.

00:22 — **Speaker UNKNOWN** will ask Jo today. The final copy **is not approved**.

## What this demonstrates

- Friday is conditional, not a confirmed final-copy deadline.
- Do not guess the product spelling from a plausible recognition result.
- “I'll” does not establish a speaker's identity when the source has no reliable speaker label.
- This fictional example shows review criteria; only listening to a real recording could verify its transcript.
